ECG Test in Jogeshwari — What It Detects and Why Doctors Recommend It

An Electrocardiogram (ECG) is one of the most commonly recommended heart tests and plays an important role in evaluating heart health. The test records the electrical activity of the heart and helps doctors identify potential cardiac problems quickly and non-invasively.

Doctors may recommend an ECG if a patient experiences symptoms such as chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, dizziness, or unexplained fatigue. The test can help detect irregular heart rhythms (arrhythmias), signs of a previous heart attack, reduced blood flow to the heart, and other abnormalities that may affect heart function.

An ECG is also commonly used as part of routine health screenings for individuals with high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or a family history of heart disease. Early detection of heart-related issues allows for timely treatment and better long-term outcomes.

If you are experiencing heart-related symptoms or have risk factors for cardiovascular disease, consulting a cardiologist in Jogeshwari can help determine whether an ECG is required. owner_posts.post_text:
Many people ignore symptoms like chest pain, breathlessness, excessive sweating, or discomfort, hoping it will pass on its own. Sometimes it's due to financial concerns, a busy schedule, fear, or simply not recognizing the warning signs.

Unfortunately, delays in seeking medical attention can turn a treatable condition into a life-threatening emergency. Our Cardiology CME highlighted the importance of early recognition of Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS), timely treatment, and effective management of cardiac emergencies—because when it comes to the heart, every minute matters.

Healing the mind is just as important as healing the body.🧠✨

When a loved one is admitted to the ICU, families often notice them becoming confused, restless, withdrawn, or unable to sleep. The reasons usually go far beyond their primary physical illness.

To shed light on this crucial aspect of patient care, Holy Spirit Hospital recently hosted a Psychiatry CME (Continuing Medical Education). Our medical professionals gathered to explore the hidden psychological challenges faced by ICU patients, emphasizing how identifying and addressing these mental health needs is a vital step toward a better, more holistic recovery.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Update: I’ve experienced both private consultation and general OPD at Holy Spirit Hospital, and overall, it has been a bad experience.

The campus itself is beautiful and well maintained. Online appointment booking is smooth, while offline booking starts at 7:30 am and doctors typically begin consultations from around 8:30 am.

The private consultation experience (ENT, in my case) was genuinely good. The doctor gave adequate time, listened patiently, and the interaction felt reassuring and professional. However, this comes at a cost, as the visit including diagnostics ended up in the range of ₹3,000–4,000.

The general OPD experience was very bad. The charges are in the range of ₹400-700.

Earlier I had positive experiences with  Gastroenterology and Surgery. I was very much impressed with the surgeon, but his opinion was outrightly dismissed by 3 other senior surgeons and physicians. I realised he kept focussing on a know problem which wasn't connected to my pain.  Gastroenterologist doesn't do any physical examination to understand the location of pain or confirm hemorrhoids. Seems, he only checks you during pricey colonoscopy and endoscopy procedures.

My experience with General Medicine and Urology OPD was disappointing. In these departments, the main doctor and an assistant doctor sit at the same small table and consult two different patients simultaneously.

In General Medicine OPD, there were up to four patients along with their attendants inside the same room at once—one with the main doctor, one with the assistant, one waiting behind the doctor, and another at the entrance being triaged for blood pressure and weight. That easily translates to 8–10 people in a single consultation room. There is no space for discussion, questions, nuance, or privacy. The doctor barely had time for eye contact, let alone a detailed conversation or examination.

In the Urology OPD, I could speak to the actual doctor only after the assistant doctor felt I was not convinced. While I do not question the competence of junior doctors, as a patient it feels unfair when you do not get adequate time with the consultant you booked.

I guess this is the truth of INR 400-700 consultations. I sincerely hope the PRO and hospital administration take note of these inconsistencies, especially given Holy Spirit’s reputation as an esteemed institution.

featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Parag,

We have carefully read your review and the multiple updates you have made over time. While we respect your right to share experiences, repeated edits with selective interpretations create confusion rather than clarity for the public.

Holy Spirit Hospital has been serving the community for over 57 years with a clear mission:
➡️ to provide ethical, quality medical care at affordable costs, especially for patients who are financially constrained.

It is important to place a few facts on record for transparency:

1️⃣ General OPD vs Private Consultation

Holy Spirit Hospital deliberately maintains low-cost General OPD consultations (₹400–₹700) so that patients from all economic backgrounds can access senior medical care. This is a conscious, charitable decision — not a compromise in quality.

Some consultants also run private OPD sessions at charges decided by them, purely for convenience and extended consultation time.
➡️ The hospital does not interfere in private OPD fees.

Comparing a low-cost charitable OPD with a private consultation model is not an apples-to-apples comparison.

2️⃣ Consultation Cost with Diagnostics

Your claim of ₹3,000–₹4,000 includes diagnostic investigations.
Any investigation—whether blood tests, imaging, or endoscopy—is:

Done only if clinically required

Clearly chargeable, as per standard medical practice anywhere in the world

This is not unique to Holy Spirit Hospital.

3️⃣ Regarding Junior Doctors

The doctors you refer to as “assistants” are not casual or unqualified staff.
They are:

Postgraduate doctors (MD/MS/DNB)

Having completed 3 years of rigorous specialty training

Working under direct supervision of senior consultants with 25–35+ years of experience

They are competent, qualified, and trained to evaluate patients thoroughly.
If a patient requests direct interaction with the senior consultant, that is always accommodated.

4️⃣ Multiple Patients in OPD Rooms

General OPD caters to high patient volumes, precisely because of its affordability. This allows thousands of patients daily—many of whom cannot afford private healthcare—to receive treatment from experienced specialists.

This model is transparent, intentional, and patient-centric, not neglectful.

5️⃣ Allegation of Doctors “Pushing Procedures”

Any invasive procedure such as endoscopy or colonoscopy is recommended only after clinical assessment, based on medical guidelines—not for revenue generation. Suggesting otherwise without evidence is a serious misrepresentation of ethical medical practice.

6️⃣ Repeated Updates to the Same Review

Repeatedly modifying the same review with escalating commentary, despite explanations, raises concerns about intent.
Constructive feedback is always welcome; repeated public reinterpretation without engagement does not help patients or institutions improve.

You have shared your Hospital ID, and we reiterate our request:
➡️ Please meet our PRO or Medical Administration so this can be discussed clinically and factually, rather than through ongoing public speculation.

Holy Spirit Hospital remains committed to:

Ethical medicine

Affordable care

Training future specialists

Serving patients who otherwise would have no access to quality healthcare

We stand by our doctors, our systems, and our mission.

Sincerely,
Holy Spirit Hospital, Andheri East

It is with immense pain that I am writing this review after losing my grandmother at KEM Hospital, Parel. Our experience was deeply distressing and disappointing.

Throughout her treatment, we felt that the doctors were not fully transparent with us. We were repeatedly given hope about her recovery, and her condition was often described as stable or improving. However, her sudden deterioration left us shocked and confused. As a family, we now feel that we were not given a clear and honest picture of how critical her situation truly was.

In such sensitive moments, families deserve clarity, honesty, and realistic guidance — even if the truth is difficult. False reassurance or incomplete communication only makes the final loss more traumatic.

The staff nurses appeared inattentive and lacked empathy during crucial times. Communication was poor, and we often had to chase for updates. The management system felt disorganized, adding unnecessary stress to an already painful situation.

Hospitals are not only about treatment; they are about compassion, accountability, and dignity. Sadly, we did not feel that our grandmother received the level of transparency and care she deserved in her final days.

I hope the hospital administration reflects seriously on patient communication, staff behavior, and overall management practices so that other families do not go through what we experienced.

Before you start off for the vaccine please carry your passport , Aadhar card and Rs. 320 in cash . All those above 60 years need to carry a fitness certificate from this family physician.
You need to enter the hospital through Gate 6 and go to the Second floor OPD 37 . The timings are from 930 am to 1230 pm (Mon to Fri) , however please note only 40 doses are given hence reaching earlier is advised. They start giving tokens at 9 am . You collect the token and go to Counter 11 on the ground floor and wait in queue to get the case paper. You are required to provide your Aadhar card here and pay 20 Rs for the case paper. You then go back to the second floor with the case paper and token and are provided a consent form which you need to fill out. Your passport will be collected and you will have to pay 300 Rs., you will be administered the dose and will have to wait for about 30 minutes while they will get the certificate ready. The certificate is a yellow card with your details and passport number written .
Please carry a water bottle and also have a breakfast before you set out to get vaccinated.
The staff is helpful but the government process is too time consuming and painful.
Thankfully you need to take this vaccine only once in your lifetime.

featured_reviews.review_text:
My father was admitted here on Sunday evening when his sugar level suddenly dropped to 25. The hospital team immediately took him to the ICU  and started treatment without any delay. I’m truly grateful to Dr. Pathare Sir, who was available even on Sunday and personally attended to him.

featured_reviews.name: Ramesh KKedar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Unethical Practices and Financial Exploitation
I am beyond disappointed with my experience at Bhatia Hospital. They seem to view patients not as people in need of care, but as opportunities for profit. During an emergency—when families are at their most vulnerable—this hospital takes full advantage by charging exorbitant, unjustified fees. I will raise this matter to health minister to take strict and worst action against hospital.

​Instead of focusing on the patient's condition, the administration is focused on the bill. It felt less like a medical facility and more like they were robbing us under the guise of "healthcare." I would strongly advise anyone in an emergency to look elsewhere unless you want to be exploited during a crisis.

Don’t waste your breath or my time trying to crawl back for forgiveness. There is absolutely nothing you can say or do that will change my mind or fix what you’ve broken. You are dead to me, and any attempt to apologize is just a pathetic insult. Stay away and keep your excuses to yourself

Their big quotes about their service and customers rights are just there for show off. But they don’t treat their customers kindly or humanly.
Not just myself, few of my other friends who have been to Bhatia Hospital for the treatment were treated really bad. I will never recommend this hospital to anybody who doesn’t live there in Mumbai.
It’s very uncomfortable to acknowledge this is not worth our time and money. Because the report which I paid for 15,000+ at Bhatia I enquired in Metropolis (across the street) it would have costed us 9000+.

featured_reviews.name: Sanaya Eranee
featured_reviews.review_text: On 18th June 2021 I went to Parsi General Hospital for my 1st dose Covishield vaccine. I was truly impressed with the way the entire process was undertaken - seamless and so well managed. I reached the Hospital at 8.30am and by exactly 8.58am I was vaccinated and seated in the wait area with a hot cup of tea given by the kind and hardworking staff. I wish to commend not only all the frontline workers, and the Team involved in this vaccination drive, but those nameless, silent faces of the Security, pantry boy and help staff all of whom went out of their way to help each and every person with courtesy, a big smile and the most polite demeanor. A Salute and Kudos to you all. I thank you very much and hope many people get to experience the wonder that is Parsi General Hospital.
